## Derivation of the Sine and Cosine Series for δ(x − ξ) on (0, ℓ)

### Setup

On the interval (0, ℓ) consider the Sturm–Liouville eigenvalue problem

$$-u'' = \lambda u, \quad 0 < x < \ell.$$

Two standard choices of self-adjoint boundary conditions yield two complete orthogonal systems on (0, ℓ) with weight w(x) = 1:

| Boundary conditions | Eigenfunctions | Norm² |
|---|---|---|
| Dirichlet: u(0)=u(ℓ)=0 | sin(nπx/ℓ), n=1,2,… | ℓ/2 |
| Neumann: u'(0)=u'(ℓ)=0 | cos(nπx/ℓ), n=0,1,2,… | ℓ (n=0), ℓ/2 (n≥1) |

Both systems are **complete** in L²(0,ℓ). In the distributional sense the delta function δ(x−ξ) (with 0 < ξ < ℓ) admits a formal expansion in each system. The coefficients are obtained by the usual Fourier projection, justified by the sifting property of δ.

---

### 1. Sine series (Dirichlet eigenfunctions)

Write

$$\delta(x-\xi) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} b_n \sin\!\left(\frac{n\pi x}{\ell}\right).$$

Project onto sin(kπx/ℓ) and use orthogonality ∫₀^ℓ sin(nπx/ℓ) sin(kπx/ℓ) dx = (ℓ/2)δ_{nk}:

$$\frac{\ell}{2}\, b_k = \int_0^\ell \delta(x-\xi)\sin\!\left(\frac{k\pi x}{\ell}\right)dx = \sin\!\left(\frac{k\pi\xi}{\ell}\right),$$

so

$$b_n = \frac{2}{\ell}\sin\!\left(\frac{n\pi\xi}{\ell}\right).$$

Hence

$$\boxed{\;\delta(x-\xi) = \frac{2}{\ell}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\sin\!\left(\frac{n\pi\xi}{\ell}\right)\sin\!\left(\frac{n\pi x}{\ell}\right),\qquad 0<x,\xi<\ell.\;}$$

---

### 2. Cosine series (Neumann eigenfunctions)

Write the half-range cosine expansion

$$\delta(x-\xi) = \frac{a_0}{2} + \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n \cos\!\left(\frac{n\pi x}{\ell}\right).$$

The coefficients are, for n ≥ 0,

$$a_n = \frac{2}{\ell}\int_0^\ell \delta(x-\xi)\cos\!\left(\frac{n\pi x}{\ell}\right)dx = \frac{2}{\ell}\cos\!\left(\frac{n\pi\xi}{\ell}\right).$$

In particular a₀ = 2/ℓ (since cos 0 = 1), so a₀/2 = 1/ℓ. Substituting:

$$\boxed{\;\delta(x-\xi) = \frac{1}{\ell} + \frac{2}{\ell}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\cos\!\left(\frac{n\pi\xi}{\ell}\right)\cos\!\left(\frac{n\pi x}{\ell}\right),\qquad 0<x,\xi<\ell.\;}$$

Equivalently, using the product-to-sum identity 2 cos A cos B = cos(A−B)+cos(A+B),

$$\delta(x-\xi) = \frac{1}{\ell}\left[1 + \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\cos\!\left(\frac{n\pi(x-\xi)}{\ell}\right) + \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\cos\!\left(\frac{n\pi(x+\xi)}{\ell}\right)\right],$$

which makes manifest the two "image" contributions at ξ and −ξ (the even reflection of the delta to the full line, period 2ℓ).

---

### 3. Verification (distributional consistency)

Both series reproduce the defining property of δ. For any test function φ ∈ C₀^∞(0,ℓ):

**Sine series.** Using the sine expansion of φ,
$$\phi(x) = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \hat\phi_n \sin\!\tfrac{n\pi x}{\ell},\quad \hat\phi_n = \tfrac{2}{\ell}\int_0^\ell \phi(\xi)\sin\!\tfrac{n\pi\xi}{\ell}\,d\xi,$$
we get
$$\int_0^\ell \!\left[\frac{2}{\ell}\sum_{n=1}^\infty \sin\!\tfrac{n\pi\xi}{\ell}\sin\!\tfrac{n\pi x}{\ell}\right]\phi(x)\,dx = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \sin\!\tfrac{n\pi\xi}{\ell}\,\hat\phi_n = \phi(\xi).$$

**Cosine series.** Using the cosine expansion of φ,
$$\phi(x) = \frac{\tilde\phi_0}{2} + \sum_{n=1}^\infty \tilde\phi_n \cos\!\tfrac{n\pi x}{\ell},\quad \tilde\phi_n = \tfrac{2}{\ell}\int_0^\ell \phi(\xi)\cos\!\tfrac{n\pi\xi}{\ell}\,d\xi,$$
we get
$$\int_0^\ell \!\left[\frac{1}{\ell}+\frac{2}{\ell}\sum_{n=1}^\infty \cos\!\tfrac{n\pi\xi}{\ell}\cos\!\tfrac{n\pi x}{\ell}\right]\phi(x)\,dx = \frac{\tilde\phi_0}{2}+\sum_{n=1}^\infty \tilde\phi_n\cos\!\tfrac{n\pi\xi}{\ell} = \phi(\xi).$$

Both reproduce φ(ξ), confirming that each series is a valid eigenfunction expansion of δ(x−ξ) on (0,ℓ). The two representations differ because they enforce different boundary behavior (odd vs. even extension to (−ℓ,ℓ)); inside the open interval (0,ℓ) both equal δ(x−ξ) in the distributional sense.

---

### Summary

$$\delta(x-\xi) = \frac{2}{\ell}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\sin\!\left(\frac{n\pi\xi}{\ell}\right)\sin\!\left(\frac{n\pi x}{\ell}\right) \qquad\text{(sine / Dirichlet series)}$$

$$\delta(x-\xi) = \frac{1}{\ell} + \frac{2}{\ell}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\cos\!\left(\frac{n\pi\xi}{\ell}\right)\cos\!\left(\frac{n\pi x}{\ell}\right) \qquad\text{(cosine / Neumann series)}$$

for 0 < x, ξ < ℓ.
